3tears-evals: read this first

Generated by uv run python packages/evals/scripts/generate_surface.py; do not edit. Names drop the
  threetears.evals. prefix. <tag> below is v and threetears.evals.__version__.

WHAT IT IS
Evals for LLM features, from a classifier to a tool-using agent: it runs each version over the same
  cases and says what moved, with the uncertainty that says whether the move is real. `Eval(cases,
  runner, grader)` says what is evaluated — the cases, the thing under test (a function, or a
  mapping of them whose first key is the control) and what counts as right (functions, field names,
  a `Judge`) — and `await ev.run()` runs it, returning a `Result` that prints quietly and writes its
  report. `python -m threetears.evals FILE` runs every eval a `.py` or `.toml` file declares.

A FIRST EVAL NEEDS AT MOST 2 NAMES
  Eval: What is evaluated: the cases, the runner under test, and what counts as right.
  Model: One model, as the engine's completion client and as three helpers for a runner of your own.
  An app that calls no model needs Eval alone: its runner is the app's own function.

YOUR APP'S CASES
Start from the cases the app already has: the data files its tests read, the tables of inputs and
  expected outputs in its test code, the examples its README or docs give. A .jsonl file (an object
  a line), a .json list of objects, a .csv with a header row or a .toml [[cases]] table loads as the
  eval's cases. Take each expected value from the app's documentation or specification, never by
  running the app or reading its code and copying what it gives: a case that expects what the app
  does today cannot catch what it does wrong. One case, whole: {"id": "double-charge", "email": "I
  was billed twice this month.", "category": "billing"}. The package keeps a case's id, stratum and
  world keys: it reads them and hands the runner and every grader the case without them.

THE FIRST EXAMPLE, WHOLE (1-triage/triage.py of the examples fetched below; its docstring left out)
  from typing import Literal

  from pydantic import BaseModel

  from threetears.evals import Eval, Model

  model = Model("deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", recording="recordings/triage.jsonl")


  class Triage(BaseModel):
      category: Literal["billing", "bug", "account", "sales", "spam"]
      urgent: bool
      needs_human: bool


  async def triage(case: dict) -> Triage:
      """Triage an inbound support email."""
      return await model.json(f"Triage this support email:\n\n{case['email']}", Triage)


  def escalates(case: dict, out: Triage) -> bool:
      """Never leaves alone an email a person must see."""
      return out.needs_human or not case["needs_human"]


  triage_eval = Eval("emails.jsonl", runner=triage, grader=["category", "urgent", escalates], k=3)
Every recorded rung replays the recordings beside it when it runs with no key, so it calls nothing
  and costs nothing, and its output is a real model's, as of that recording.
Each email is triaged k=3 times; it replays `recordings/triage.jsonl` offline, and `RECORD=1` with
  `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set records it again.

GETTING THE EXAMPLES: they are not in the installed package; fetch them from the repository
  git clone --depth 1 --branch <tag> --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/pacepace/3tears
  cd 3tears && git sparse-checkout set packages/evals/examples && cd packages/evals/examples
Then run one from that fetched directory: python -m threetears.evals 1-triage/triage.py. Each rung
  reads its cases and replays its recordings from beside itself, so keep its directory together.

READING WHAT COMES BACK
The first line printed is the answer. Rung 1 prints:
  emails: triage passed 70 of 90 trials on 30 cases. Cases that failed a trial: double-charge,
    refund-after-cancel, gdpr-delete, book-demo, phish-suspend, and 7 more.
A comparison prints what to do (contrasts()'s "advice": to a v2 no better (worse by more than a
  margin, given one): switch at most 1 time in 3, 1 in 10 with undo="hard"), then what is proven:
  compare: Advice: keep v1. v2 is behind it.
  compare: Accuracy: v2 behind v1, proof pending. Over 30 paired cases, v2 is 1 point behind v1. The
    interval allows v2 to be as much as 14 points worse or 12 better. The evidence that v2 is worse
    is weak (1.2). Of 90 trials each, Accuracy was right on 90 for v1 and 89 for v2.
Run again with cases appended, it continues, its error kept; a runner or grader is known by its name
  (a judge by model and criteria), not its code: rename it to compare an edit.
Below: each measure's rate, the top misses and why, where the report is. A refusal goes to stderr,
  exit 2; an action that refuses answers with refused: and a remedy:.
  Exit codes: 0 Every run completed and graded an answer; 1 A run did not complete, or no arm had an
    answer graded; 2 Refused before it ran: the file, or what it declares; 3 An error nothing
    anticipated, its traceback printed; 4 A comparison's gate failed, with a line saying why.

LATER TASKS, BY RUNG (https://github.com/pacepace/3tears/blob/<tag>/packages/evals/docs/ladder.md)
  Rung 2, a judge, checked against a person: Judge, Example
  Rung 3, two prompts, compared: grader
  Rung 4, an agent, graded on the world it leaves: World, quick.as_host,
    transports.fastmcp.mount_fastmcp
  Rung 5, evaluate the evaluator: harness.AnalystSkill, harness.Writer, harness.WriterEval
  Off the ladder, taught on a page: Answer
    (https://github.com/pacepace/3tears/blob/<tag>/packages/evals/docs/cost-and-budgets.md)

EMBEDDING IT IN AN APP (https://github.com/pacepace/3tears/blob/<tag>/packages/evals/docs/adopting-a-host.md)
  A product builds one kernel.host.EvalHost and hands it to every entrypoint. The 18 ports a host
    may implement: schema.AsyncDocumentStore, schema.AsyncStoreClock, schema.BoundCompletionClient,
    schema.CompletionClient, schema.CompletionResult, schema.DocumentStore,
    schema.ProviderFailureDescriber, schema.StoreClock, schema.ToolTurnClient, schema.TraceSink,
    kernel.ActionSeam, kernel.CandidateKind, kernel.DeliverySeam, kernel.Recordable,
    kernel.host.CompletionClients, run.CellExecutor, run.KindFactory, providers.Pricer.
  Every declared name, with one line each:
    https://github.com/pacepace/3tears/blob/<tag>/packages/evals/docs/surface.md

NEEDS A SHIPPED EXAMPLE (#1199): the only door to each; no shipped example uses it yet
  kernel.failed_call_output: A host's own kind routes a failed call through it, so an account
    refusal stops the run, a decline excludes the cell and an unserved model is never judged.
  kernel.host.MemberActsOn: A host marks a map field of its kind's overlay with it, so each entry is
    attributed to what it acts on.
  kernel.host.Ordinal: A host marks a `Literal` or `Enum` knob of its kind's overlay with it, so the
    knob's values are ranked.
  ops.start_action_job: A host's own action runs work that is not one paid call as a job through it
    (`start_paid_call` covers one paid call).

KINDS: every declared name is one; the surface page named above lists each under its kind
  typed: a newcomer writes it in an eval file.
  bound: a host implements it or hands it to the engine.
  action: the function behind a catalogue action, which an agent or operator invokes by name.
  invoked: a function a host's own code calls, to make the engine act or do one step its way.
  received: a value someone is handed and reads.
  tests: a kit, recorder or guard a host runs in its own tests.
